These have the most prospects of producing architectural-scale components without the needs for extremely large hardware. I'm waiting on a laser cutter whose shipment has long been delayed. I was saving up for a CNC router, but that's been put on hold lately. I've also built various hydroponics and Living Wall setups. I've long studied Post-Industrial technology and the many forms of digital fabrication and been working toward assembling my own fab lab. I'd like to get into CNC fabrication of Tiny Houses, relief housing, and furnitecture. (that's furniture which bridges the line between furniture and architecture through the use of volumetric multifunctional structures)

The home I imagine, and hope to build, in the future is furnitecture based. Essentially, a minimalist pavilion with clear and translucent enclosure panels and a totally open plan interior that uses furnitecture structures to define the functional zones. So, instead of rooms you have free-standing 'pods' or 'frames' that assume the different functions of the home and can be fully portable, moved around the home, or easily redesigned and replaced like appliances as your needs change. These would also include some atypical functions like hydroponics pods, server and telecom rack pods, CAVEs (CAVE automatic virtual environment), and digital machine tool workstations. Such a home would also be well suited to experimental domestic robot use as it is would be single storey and free of the many barriers to robot movement common with a conventional house.
